query: In `release/unix/make_scripts_portable.py`, explain how `main` rewrites the installed scripts so they keep working when the Python distribution is moved: which files it touches, how it recognises a script header, what it does with a matching interpreter path, and when it leaves a file alone.

operations.name: Directory entries that are not regular files are skipped
A file whose first non-blank line is not a comment is treated as a binary and stops processing
A header that points at this interpreter is replaced by the portable shebang
expressions: data.write(portable_shebang if executable == interpreter else line)

operations.name: A file that produced no content is left untouched

dependencies.name: Only headers under the interpreter's own directory are considered; any other header line is copied unchanged
The executable named in the header is resolved and compared with this interpreter before replacing
The rest of the file after the header is appended unchanged and the result is collected before the emptiness check
